sources.citation: Bril, I., C. Moyse-Faurie, F. Ozanne-Rivierre, J.-C. Rivierre (LACITO-CNRS), updated S. Bearune, A.-L. Dotte, S. Geneix-Rabault (ERALO-UNC). 2021. Bibliographie sur les langues de Nouvelle-Calédonie, Arhö entry p. 23.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. States that Arhö has 'Pas de tradition d'écriture et peu de documentation scientifique': the first lexical survey is Leenhardt 1946 ('Aro', n° 3) preceded by a few pages of linguistic notes (pp. 29-33); Leenhardt's lexicon was revised by A.-G. Haudricourt in his 1963 survey; a brief survey and recordings were made by J.-C. Rivierre in 1994. No other work listed.

sources.citation: Leenhardt, Maurice. 1946. Langues et dialectes de l'Austro-Mélanésie. Paris: Institut d'Ethnologie (Travaux et Mémoires XLVI). Chapter '3. — ARO', pp. 29-33 (Gallica ark:/12148/bpt6k21694f, views f76-f80).
sources.note: The Arhö chapter has a '§ 2. — Accent et ton' paragraph (p. 29) but it states no accent placement at all: it only says Poya is a linguistic crossroads and that 'l'articulation de l'ARO rappelle celle des langues de Bourail'. The book's general phonetics conclusion (p. 11) defers accent and tone to each language chapter. For the neighbouring languages the same author gives a rule: Ajië p. 13 'accent tonique léger sur la dernière syllabe du mot plein' (compounds keep the accent on the full word); Arhâ p. 25 'Accent comme celui de l'AJIË'; Boewe (Bourail) p. 34 'L'accent est le même qu'en AJIË'…

sources.note: Nothing on phonology; 349 speakers over 14 (ISEE 2009), Poya region, 'fortement menacé'; corpus item is a counting text only.

sources.citation: Lionnet, Florian. ICHL26 handout 'Accent and tone: the double origin of the Paicî tone system'.
sources.note: About Paicî/Xârâcùù accent and tone only (citing Rivierre 1978); Arhö not mentioned.

Nothing on stress; 'Arho is often considered as an Ajië dialect. No existing tradition of script.' Bibliography lists only general NC works (Leenhardt 1946, Haudricourt 1971, Haudricourt et al. 1979, Rivierre 1981 Atlas notice, etc.).
No phonology; the fr infobox labels the language 'Langue à tons' with no source (unsupported; not usable).

sources.citation: Rivierre, Jean-Claude. 1994. Unpublished brief field survey and recordings of Arhö (Poya) (reported in the LACITO/UNC Bibliographie sur les langues de Nouvelle-Calédonie 2021, p. 23).
